From: Orchid AI Prod Team <prod@orchid.ai>

Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 15:23:00 +0000
Subject: Live chat responses very slow since 15:20 UTC — urgent

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing severe latency on the streaming/chat API around 15:20 UTC. Conversation responses are arriving in large, infrequent chunks (10–20s gaps), which is breaking our live support experience. Impact: ~30% of sessions in us-west-2 experiencing >8s per chunk and occasional stalls.

We have a high-visibility cohort starting at 16:00 UTC and need immediate mitigation guidance — ideally a short list of workarounds we can apply now and an ETA for a fix. I've attached a short telemetry snippet and a sample client trace that shows long server-side token generation pauses.

What we need:
- A quick mitigation we can enable on our side (short-term config change)
- Confirmation of whether this is a known platform issue or something specific to our account/region
- Any temporary routing or model fallbacks you can push for us

We appreciate quick help — our support team is monitoring and I can hop on a call if easier (link: https://meet.orchid.ai/hot).

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform
Orchid AI

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Orchid AI Prod Team <prod@orchid.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 15:35:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Live chat responses very slow since 15:20 UTC — urgent

Samira — thanks for the heads-up and the telemetry. We see the same signal in our edge telemetry for us-west-2 and have opened ticket RI-7821. Short answer: we will (1) put temporary routing in front of your traffic to bypass the affected shard, (2) recommend a quick client-side fallback you can enable immediately, and (3) deploy a targeted hotfix to affected edge nodes. Timeline: routing change started at 15:40 UTC; hotfix roll expected by 17:00 UTC.

Immediate workarounds you can apply now (low-friction):
- Switch to non-streaming (polling) responses for sessions that can tolerate slight latency but need reliability: set streaming=false and poll with a 500ms backoff.
- Reduce max_tokens to 250 for high-concurrency endpoints to lower per-request compute pressure.
- If you use a streaming client, set client param stream_chunk_timeout=2000ms to avoid waiting for large chunks and to show incremental UI updates.
- Optionally pin requests to the smaller generation variant (model: redwood-medium-v1) for live support cohorts.

We're pushing a temporary route that should reduce the chunk gaps; please confirm if you see improvement in the next 10–15 minutes. I'll keep Ben, Marissa, and Dylan looped for credits, customer comms, and infra action.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchid.ai>, Orchid AI Prod Team <prod@orchid.ai>

Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 19:05:00 +0000
Subject: Post-incident update & next steps — RI-7821 (Orchid AI)

Hi Samira — thanks again for the patience and for sharing traces. Below is a concise post-incident summary, what we changed to mitigate, and the permanent actions we will take. TL;DR: root cause was an edge encoder regression that increased CPU stall time for long-context streaming requests; temporary routing + rolling hotfix restored normal chunk cadence.

What happened (timeline):
- 15:20 UTC — Orchid reports increased chunk gaps and stalls. Customer telemetry matches platform edge signals.
- 15:40 UTC — We applied a temporary routing rule to route Orchid traffic to healthy edge shards; customer reports partial improvement.
- 16:30 UTC — Infra identified tokenizer/encoder path increased CPU blocking on a subset of nodes during long-context sessions.
- 17:05 UTC — We deployed a targeted hotfix and performed rolling restarts for affected edge nodes. Normal streaming cadence restored by 17:20 UTC.

Short-term mitigation (already completed):
- Temporary routing to bypass affected shard (15:40–17:20 UTC).
- Rolling hotfix and restart of impacted edge nodes (17:05–17:20 UTC).
- Customer workarounds we recommended: non-streaming polling fallback, reduced max_tokens, model pinning to redwood-medium-v1 — used by Orchid during the incident for some cohorts.

Impact and customer support:
- We estimate ~3.5 hours of degraded user experience window (start-to-recovery overhead included); your production cohort saw intermittent degradation primarily between 15:20–17:20 UTC.
- Ben will follow up with a formal credit proposal (ticket RI-7821) and coordinate the statement for your finance/procurement team.

Permanent actions we will take:
- Revert the regression in the encoder/tokenizer code path and add a safety gate to block risky runtime changes from reaching edge pools without extended load tests.
- Improve edge telemetry to detect token-generation stalls earlier and trigger automated failover faster.
- Update our streaming SDK docs with recommended client-side fallbacks (polling and chunk-timeout param guidance).

Attachments and links:
- Post-incident summary (attachment): orchid_postmortem_summary.pdf
- Support ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/RI-7821
- Postmortem draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/u/0/folders/PM-RI-7821

Next steps:
- Ben: expect a proposed goodwill credit and short customer note by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa: I will schedule a 30–45 minute postmortem call with your engineers — propose windows 48 hours out, please let us know availability.
- Dylan and infra: we'll push the encoder rollback to staging + extended soak and keep you updated.

If you'd like a synchronous run-through, I'm available for a quick call. We regret the disruption and appreciate the detailed traces you provided — they significantly sped up root cause identification.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
